title: The power is out
short: First steps, light, medicines, lifts, generators
intro: Readings for a power cut that may last hours or days: the first steps at home, staying informed, medicines that need power or cold, lifts, generators, and what to do when the power comes back.

choices.label: The power just went out
choices.hint: A power cut or a blackout: dark at home and next door, no idea for how long

read.label: What to do in a blackout, in order
read.note: In German. Stay calm, check whether it is only your street, radio on, tell the family, unplug devices, leave one lamp on.

read.label: First steps at home
read.note: In German. Family, devices, the radio, water, light, the lift, the freezer, vital medicines, waste and a substitute toilet.

read.label: How to behave during a blackout
read.note: In Italian. Switch off appliances, keep the fridge shut, listen to the radio, avoid lifts, and generator safety.

choices.label: Cooking and the fridge without power
Staying warm without heating
choices.hint: In the guide on heat and cold

choices.label: Someone needs power or cold for a medicine or a device
choices.hint: Insulin, a breathing machine, oxygen, a powered wheelchair

read.label: Vital medicines in a blackout
read.note: In German. Check how long they will last; insulin must be kept cool; if they will not last a week, whom to tell.

read.label: Life-sustaining devices that need power
read.note: In Italian. Ask for help early: in Italy the page names 118 and the social services.

read.label: Spare batteries and chargers for aids
read.note: In German. Aids that need power, a medicines plan and stock, and who can help you leave if you must.

choices.hint: Someone may be trapped, stairs only

read.label: Check the lift for trapped people
read.note: In German. Among the steps for the building and the street: the lift, neighbours, and people who need help.

read.label: Do not use the lift until power is back for good
read.note: In Italian. Power may come and go while repairs are made.

choices.label: I want to run a generator
choices.hint: A portable generator, fuel, where to put it

read.label: Generators: where to run them, fuel, fire risk
read.note: In German. Never in closed rooms; about a litre of fuel an hour; stored fuel is a fire risk. Also why solar panels usually stop too.

read.label: Plug devices into the generator, not the house
read.note: In Italian. Do not connect it to the home's wiring, and never start it in the house or the garage.

read.label: No generator or outdoor heater inside the home

choices.label: It could last for days
choices.hint: Shops shut, no cash machines, no phones, staying at home

read.label: What a long blackout means
read.note: In German. Shops close, medical care gets harder by the hour, homes cool down, no lift or phone, waste piles up.

read.label: What stops working without power
read.note: In German. Phones and internet, card payments and cash machines, fridge, stove, tap water, lights, heating.

read.label: Stay at home and look after each other
read.note: In German. Stay home unless you are needed, save fuel, talk with neighbours, find who needs help.

choices.label: The power is back
choices.hint: What to switch on, phone calls, heating

read.label: After a blackout
read.note: In German. Check the stove and iron are off, switch on only what you need, avoid calls that are not urgent.

read.label: When the power returns
read.note: In German. Devices, heating, fridge, sewage pumps, cash, staying at home, and waiting before restarting computers.

limits.text: Call the emergency numbers only for a life-threatening emergency.
A generator has an engine: it cannot be run in closed rooms, and stored fuel is a fire risk.
Do not connect a generator to the home's wiring, and never start it inside the house or the garage.
Avoid lifts until the power is declared restored: it may come and go during repairs.
If vital medicines such as insulin will not last a week, tell a pharmacy, a doctor or the ambulance service.
Never leave candles or other open flames unattended.
When the power returns, check that the stove and the iron are really off: they can start a fire.

prepare.label: What to keep at home for a blackout
prepare.note: In German. Water, food, a battery or crank radio, lights, medicines, a way to cook, cash in small notes; plan for 10 to 14 days.

prepare.label: Get ready as for a camping trip
prepare.note: In German. Shut-off valves, what your town has planned, one to two weeks of food and water.
